rows.name: Rocco Arena
rows.note: THE KEY RECORD. Age 39 in March 1900 and indexed year of birth 1861 -- which CONFIRMS the family tree's birth year for Rocco Arena, and does so from a source entirely independent of it. Recorded as a US CITIZEN, so he had naturalised: he was in America years before this, and his son Antonio was born at New York in 1895. THE 1900 IMAGE HAS NOW BEEN READ: line 27 of the S.S. Trave, 'Arena Rocco', 39, married, SAILOR -- matching the marinaro of act 22 of 1893 -- nationality 'Citizen U.S.A.', last residence SCILLA, carrying $50. NOTE FOR ANYONE REPEATING THIS: the 1900 form has NO parental columns, so it cannot name his father. That question needs a different record.

rows.name: Anna Arena
rows.note: THE IMAGE NAMES HER RELATIONSHIP. Line 4 of the manifest does not begin with her surname but with the word 'NIECE' -- 'Niece, Anna Arena', 6, occupation 'none'. She is the niece of the Giovanni Arena on the line above, who is himself going to join 'brother Rocco'. The document therefore states, twice over, that Giovanni is Rocco's brother and Anna is Rocco's daughter. The tree puts her crossing in 1894 aged one; it was 23 May 1899, aged six, and she was brought over by her uncle.

rows.name: Giovanni Arena
rows.note: THE IMAGE HAS NOW BEEN READ AND IT NAMES THE RELATIONSHIPS OUTRIGHT. Line 3: Arena Giovanni, 45, SAILOR, going to join -- in the column for whether the passenger joins a relative -- 'BROTHER ROCCO, N. YORK, MULBERRY ST'. So GIOVANNI ARENA IS ROCCO ARENA'S BROTHER, a sibling the family tree does not have, and Rocco was living on MULBERRY STREET, New York, in May 1899. His age of 45 matches the Arena Giovanni born at Scilla on 20 April 1854 exactly -- though that act names the mother Rosa Arlotta where Rocco's is Serafina Arlotta, which is the one loose end.

rows.name: Michele Donato
rows.note: THE IMAGE HAS NOW BEEN READ. S.S. LIGURIA, sailing from PALERMO on 22 FEBRUARY 1908. Line 15, no. 130: DONATO MICHELE, aged 52, male, married, SAILOR, Italian, South Calabria, last permanent residence SCILLA. Nearest relative in the country whence he came: 'WIFE MARIA SOFI, VIA GROTTE, SCILLA' -- confirming his wife AND the street from act 162 of 1892 (Via Grotte 31), from a document filled in on another continent sixteen years later. Final destination: QUINCY, FLORIDA. His age of 52 is the THIRD independent witness to a birth about 1856 against the tree's 1851.

rows.name: Giuseppe Polistena
rows.note: Candidate for the tree's Giuseppi Polistena b. 1875, Giovanni Polistena's elder brother. Two years out on the age, which is ordinary.

rows.name: Maria Polistena
rows.note: On the line immediately after Giuseppe -- a married couple travelling together.

rows.name: Giovanni Donato
rows.note: LINE 2 -- immediately after Annunziata Polistena. A Polistena and a Donato teenager side by side on one manifest in 1903, nine years before Giovanni Polistena married Nunziata Donato. The families were already travelling together.

rows.name: Pasquale Donato
rows.note: Same ship, same frame as Lorenjo Costa two lines below.

rows.name: Lorenjo Costa
rows.note: Two lines below Pasquale Donato. Costa is Generosa Costa's surname; Donato is Michele's.

rows.name: Domenica Anile
rows.note: EXACT. The tree gives her birth as 20 February 1880, which makes her twenty-six on 2 August 1906. She is line 27 of a family group occupying five consecutive lines. THE IMAGE HAS NOW BEEN READ. The party of five is braced together and the 'going to join' column names one man for all of them: 'DOMENICO MELLUSO, 2173 FIRST AVE, N.Y.' The relationship words across the group are brother-or-mother, HUSBAND, FATHER, FATHER, COUSIN. So Domenica Anile was going to her HUSBAND -- which the family tree already says, and which the manifest now confirms -- and the two small boys were going to their FATHER. The name column carries only two written surnames, ANILE for the women and MELLUSO for the children, with ditto braces, which is how the index came to give a Melluso child an Anile surname. CAVEAT: the exact line-to-word alignment of the relationship column is not certain, because the brace spans several rows. The destination and the husband are.

rows.name: Fillipo Melluso

rows.name: Concetta Anile
rows.note: The tree gives her birth as 1888, which would make her eighteen. The manifest says twenty-one. She is the only Concetta Anile on the voyage and the tree already claimed this exact arrival date and the port of Naples, so it is her with the age overstated -- which was routine for a young woman travelling without her parents. rows.name: Francesco Melluso
rows.note: ONE YEAR OLD, line 29, closing the group -- and the image shows he is NOT an Anile. The name column writes MELLUSO against the children with a ditto brace; only the women are written Anile. He is Domenica Anile's younger son by Domenico Melluso, travelling to his father at 2173 First Avenue. NOT IN THE FAMILY TREE. The index gave him his mother's maiden surname, exactly as it did his brother Filippo, who it indexed as 'Foloppo Melluso Anile'.

rows.name: Filippo Melluso
rows.note: A SECOND Filippo Melluso of Briatico on the same ship, aged thirteen, four lines and two frames earlier. Not the tree's man, who is the three-year-old. Recorded so that nobody later merges them.

rows.name: Giovanni Polistena
rows.note: ON THE LINE IMMEDIATELY AFTER MICHELE DONATO. Aged 24, single, SAILOR, of Scilla -- which fits his birth on 16 September 1883 exactly. Nearest relative: 'FATHER ANTONINO POLISTENA AND MOTHER GIOVANNA ROMANO, SCILLA'. THAT SETTLES THE OLDEST CONFLICT IN THIS ARCHIVE: the family tree calls his mother Giovanna PONTILLO; act 206 of 1883 says Giovanna ROMANO; and now a US immigration manifest, taken from his own statement twenty-five years later and half a world away, says GIOVANNA ROMANO. Destination: QUINCY, FLORIDA. The tree records no crossing for him at all. He would marry Michele Donato's daughter Nunziata about eight years after they sailed together.

rows.name: Rocco Arena
rows.residence: Citizen of the U.S. of A., New York
rows.note: HIS THIRD RECORDED CROSSING, and it confirms the family tree twice over. The tree gives Rocco Arena a departure from MESSINA and an arrival on 12 SEPTEMBER 1913: the manifest says Messina and 11 September -- right port, one day out. He is 52 and again entered as a US CITIZEN, so still naturalised thirteen years after the Trave. Age 52 in September 1913 gives a birth about 1861, the same answer the 1900 manifest gave and the same one-year overshoot against act 228's 20 December 1861. Three crossings are now known: 1892 (per the 1900 census), 21 March 1900 on the Trave, and this one. AND HE WAS NOT ALONE: ROCCO POLISTENA, 44, of Scilla, is on the SAME SHIP the SAME DAY, four frames away at T715-2174 frame 292, line 19. An Arena and a Polistena crossing together in 1913 -- and a generation later Anna Arena's son Rocco married Angela Polistena.

cohort.note: Twenty-one Arena gave Scilla as their last residence at Ellis Island. Among them an ORAZIO Arena (20 April 1904, aged 26) and four men named Rocco.

Fifteen Donato gave Scilla as their last residence -- which settles one thing outright: the Donato were unquestionably a Scilla family by the 1890s, whatever the birth registers of the 1850s do not say.
Six Polistena, including a married couple and two teenagers.
Four Costa. No Generosa among them.
Fourteen Melluso gave Briatico as their last residence, including two different Filippo.
Thirteen Anile, five of them on one ship on one day.
